d: Piazza di Aquileja. The night, near the end, is lighted by a large amount of torches. All around it is a miserable heap of ruins. Here and there I still see stretch rise some flame, residue of a horrible four-day fire. The scene is cluttered by Unni, Eruli, Ostrogothi, etc.
Attila is led over a cart pulled by the slaves, dukes, kings, etc.
Uldin, Odabella, Virgins of Aquileja and sayings.
Ezio, Roman officers, and sayings.
Attila, and Ezio.

Rio-Alto in the Adriatic lagoons. Here and there above palafittes rise some huts, communicating with each other for the long axis supported by boats. On the front stands in a similar way an altar of stones dedicated to St. James. Further on I glimpsed a bell hanging from a wooden cottage, which was then the bell tower of St. James. The darkness goes thinning among the stormy clouds: then a little by little a rose light, until (on the finish of the scene) the immediate ray of the sun flooding for everything, the firmament of the most serene and clear blue. The slow touch of the bell greets the morning. Some Hermits come out from the huts and start at the altar.
From the ships, which slowly arrive, come out Forest, Women, Men and Children of Aquileja, etc.
Wood by the camp of Attila. It is night; in the nearby stream the rays of the moon shine. Odabel alone.
Forest, in barbarian costume, and said.

Attila's tent. Above the ground, covered by a skin of tiger, is lying down Uldino sleeping. At the bottom, on the left, by means of a curtain raised in the middle, which forms like a secluded room, I saw Attila sleeping on the very low oriental bed, and also covered with tiger skins.
Attila alone.
Uldin, Druids, Dukes, Kings and sayings.

The camp of Attila. From the hill at the bottom, you can see progress, preceded by Leo and by six Elders, processionally a group of Virgins and Children in white robes bearing palms. The scene is cluttered by the hosts of Attila in arms. Among the multitude there is Foresto with lowered visor, Odabella, and sayings.
Campo d'Ezio. Scorgesi in the distance the great city of the seven hills. Ezio alone. He comes out holding in his hand an explained papyrus and showing spite.
Preceded by some Roman Soldiers I presented a matte of Attila's Schiavi, and said.
Among the Slaves who leave one remained. He is Forest.
I'm lonely.

Campo d'Attila as in the first act, prepared for solemn banquet. The night is brightened by a hundred flames bursting with large oak trunks prepared for it. Hunni, Ostrogoths, Eruli, etc. While the Warriors sing, Attila, followed by the Druids, the Priestsses, the Dukes and Kings, goes to sit in his place. Odabella is near him in the costume of amazon.
Uldin, Forestus, who once again in a warrior dress is mixed with the multitude, and said.
Bosco as in the first act, which divides the camp of Attila from that of Ezio. It is the morning. Forest alone. Indi Uldino.
Lonely.
That said, and Ezio, who is hasty on the side of the Roman camp.
Odabella, always in amazon tools with royal mantle and crown, which is frightened and fleeing from the barbarian camp, and sayings.
Attila, who goes straight to Odabella, and sayings.
Roman warriors, breaking in everywhere, and sayings.
